descripcion_es: Bookings, the airport, the hotel and problems during a trip.
resumen: Words and phrases for booking, getting around an airport or station, staying in a hotel and solving travel problems.

explicacion.texto: Travel is the verb (to go from place to place) and the general concept; trip is a specific journey somewhere (a business trip); journey is the time spent going from one place to another (the journey takes two hours). You do not say “a travel”.

filas: I booked a room for three nights.
a ticket for going only / for going and coming back (es: billete de ida / de ida y vuelta)
A return ticket to York, please.
to register on arrival / to leave the hotel (es: registrarse / dejar el hotel)
the card that lets you get on the plane (es: tarjeta de embarque)
Show your boarding pass at the gate.
the door where you get on the plane (es: puerta de embarque)
the bags you travel with; uncountable (es: equipaje)
How much luggage do you have?
the bags you take on the plane with you (es: equipaje de mano)
Only one piece of hand luggage.
Our flight was delayed by two hours.
to arrive too late to catch a flight / train (es: perder un vuelo / tren)
to leave the ground / to come down to the ground (es: despegar / aterrizar)
the place where you get on a train (es: andén)
a room with one big bed / for one person / with two beds (es: habitación doble / individual / con dos camas)
I have booked a room (es: Tengo una reserva)
I have a reservation under the name Pérez.
Do I pay extra for breakfast? (es: ¿Está incluido el desayuno?)
Is breakfast included in the price?
with no rooms or seats left (es: completo)
Sorry, the hotel is fully booked.
The … is broken (es: El/la … no funciona)
to be unable to find / bags that have gone missing (es: perder / equipaje perdido)
visiting famous places as a tourist (es: turismo, visitar monumentos)
a visit with a guide (es: visita guiada)
Is there a guided tour in Spanish?

items: Luggage and baggage are uncountable: a suitcase / a piece of luggage.
To be too late for a means of transport is miss; to be unable to find an object is lose.
Go on holiday (British) = go on vacation (American).

ejemplos.frase: I'd like to book a double room for the weekend.
ejemplos.traduccion: Querría reservar una habitación doble para el fin de semana.

ejemplos.frase: Our flight was cancelled because of the storm.
ejemplos.traduccion: Nos cancelaron el vuelo por la tormenta.

ejemplos.frase: We missed the bus and had to take a taxi.
ejemplos.traduccion: Perdimos el autobús y tuvimos que coger un taxi.

ejemplos.frase: The journey from Madrid to Barcelona takes about three hours.
ejemplos.traduccion: El trayecto de Madrid a Barcelona dura unas tres horas.

ejemplos.frase: Excuse me, the shower in my room doesn't work.
ejemplos.traduccion: Perdone, la ducha de mi habitación no funciona.

ejemplos.frase: She went on a business trip to Singapore.
ejemplos.traduccion: Fue a Singapur en viaje de negocios.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: We had a wonderful travel to Peru.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: We had a wonderful trip to Peru.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: A specific journey is a trip; travel is mainly a verb.
Being too late for transport is miss.

errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I have three suitcases / pieces of luggage.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I want to reserve a habitation.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I want to book a room.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Spanish “habitación” is room; habitation is the act of living somewhere.

ejercicios.frase: Hurry up or we'll ___ the plane!
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that being too late for a means of transport is miss and losing an object is lose (both are “perder” in Spanish). The clue is “the plane”: it is about not getting to a means of transport on time. That is why we'll miss the plane. After will comes the infinitive without to or -s.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Being too late for transport is miss.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Lose is to be unable to find an object (lose your keys); not getting to transport on time is miss.
Loose is an adjective (“not tight”); besides, for transport the verb is miss.
After will ('ll) comes the infinitive, miss, not the past.

glosario.significado: perder (un transporte), no llegar a tiempo

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete: the place where you wait for a train (es: “andén”).
ejercicios.frase: The train to Leeds leaves from ___ 6.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card gives platform for Spanish “andén”. The clue is the train next to the number 6: in a station trains leave from a numbered platform. At the airport the equivalent would be gate, where you board the plane; the two words are not interchangeable.
ejercicios.traduccion: El tren a Leeds sale del andén 6.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Gate is the boarding door at an airport; at the station it is platform.
The English word is required: platform.

ejercicios.frase: You must check ___ before 11 o'clock on the day you leave.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card includes check in, “to register on arrival”, and check out, “to leave the hotel”. The clue is “on the day you leave”: it is about leaving the hotel, so it is check out. Note that the phrasal verb is written as two words (check out) and the noun with a hyphen (check-out).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Leaving the hotel is check out.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tiene que dejar la habitación antes de las 11 el día que se vaya.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Check in is registering when you arrive; when you leave it is check out.
Check off is ticking items on a list; for leaving the hotel you use out.

glosario.significado: dejar la habitación, pagar y salir del hotel

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete: going and coming back (es: “ida y vuelta”).
ejercicios.frase: A ___ ticket to Bristol, please. I'm coming back tonight.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card distinguishes a single ticket, for going only, and a return ticket, for going and coming back. The clue is “I'm coming back tonight”: the person goes and comes back. In British English you say return; in American English, round-trip (also without a hyphen). That is why all three forms are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Going and coming back is return (British) or round-trip (American).
ejercicios.traduccion: Un billete de ida y vuelta a Bristol, por favor. Vuelvo esta noche.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A single ticket is for going only; the person is coming back that night.
Calque of Spanish “ida y vuelta”; you say return or round-trip.
Double is used for rooms, not for return tickets.

ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that trip is a specific journey, while travel is mainly the verb or the general concept and you do not say “a travel”. The clue is your … to Japan: a particular journey, with a destination. That is why How was your trip?
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A specific journey is a trip.

por_opcion.trip: Correct: trip is a specific journey, going somewhere and coming back (a trip to Japan).
por_opcion.travel: Incorrect: travel is the verb or the general concept (I love travel); it is not used for a specific journey.
por_opcion.voyage: Incorrect in this context: voyage is a long journey by sea or through space, with a literary tone.

ejercicios.frase: The plane can't ___ off because of the fog.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card gives take off, “to leave the ground”, and land, “to come down to the ground”. The clue is the plane with the particle off already written: the fixed phrasal verb for leaving the ground is take off. Neither get off nor go off has that meaning.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A plane leaving the ground is take off.
ejercicios.traduccion: El avión no puede despegar por la niebla.

por_opcion.take: Correct: take off is what a plane does when it leaves the ground.
por_opcion.get: Incorrect: get off is getting out of a vehicle (get off the bus), not leaving the ground.
por_opcion.go: Incorrect: go off means an alarm ringing, food going bad or something exploding; not a plane leaving the ground.

ejercicios.frase: Sorry, we have no rooms left. The hotel is fully ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card includes fully booked for Spanish “completo”. The clue is “we have no rooms left”: all the rooms are reserved. Fully booked literally means “totally reserved”. Complete is a false friend in this context.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A hotel with no rooms left is fully booked.
ejercicios.traduccion: Lo siento, no nos quedan habitaciones. El hotel está completo.

por_opcion.booked: Correct: fully booked means “full, with no places left”.
por_opcion.complete: Incorrect: complete means finished or whole; you do not say fully complete for a full hotel.
por_opcion.busy: Incorrect: busy means “crowded, full of activity”; a hotel can be busy and still have free rooms.

ejercicios.frase: The airline ___ my suitcase and I had no clothes.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that losing an object is lose (past lost), while miss is kept for transport. The clue is my suitcase: a suitcase is an object that goes missing. That is why The airline lost my suitcase.
ejercicios.traduccion: La aerolínea me perdió la maleta y me quedé sin ropa.

por_opcion.lost: Correct: lose (lost) is to be unable to find an object, to mislay it.
por_opcion.missed: Incorrect: miss is being too late for transport or feeling sad that someone is not there; a suitcase is not “missed”.
por_opcion.forgot: Incorrect: forget means not remembering; the airline did not forget the suitcase, it lost it.

ejercicios.frase: How many luggages are you taking?
respuestas: How much luggage are you taking?
ejercicios.explicacion: The card warns that luggage and baggage are uncountable. The clue is “How many luggages”: many and the plural only work with countable nouns. With an uncountable noun you ask how much and the noun stays singular: How much luggage are you taking? To count items you say suitcases or pieces of luggage.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Luggage is uncountable: how much luggage.

errores_previstos.respuesta: How many luggages are you taking?
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: luggage is uncountable.

errores_previstos.respuesta: How many luggage are you taking?
errores_previstos.explicacion: The plural is removed, but many is still for countable nouns; you need much.

errores_previstos.respuesta: How much luggages are you taking?
errores_previstos.explicacion: Luggage has no plural.

ejercicios.frase: We lost the last bus and walked home.
respuestas: We missed the last bus and walked home.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule on the card: being too late for a means of transport is miss. The clue is the last bus: they did not get to the bus on time; they did not mislay it. That is why We missed the last bus. Lose is only used for objects (lose your keys) or for games (lose a match).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Being too late for a bus is miss.
ejercicios.traduccion: Perdimos el último autobús y volvimos a casa andando.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We lost the last bus and walked home.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: you miss transport, you do not lose it.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We miss the last bus and walked home.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The correct verb is miss, but the past is missing: missed.

ejercicios.frase: I'd like a habitation with a sea view.
respuestas: I'd like a room with a sea view.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the false friend on the card: habitation is not Spanish “habitación”, but the act of living somewhere or an inhabited place (formal). The clue is the hotel context: “a … with a sea view”. A room in a hotel or a house is room.
ejercicios.traduccion: Querría una habitación con vistas al mar.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'd like a habitation with a sea view.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: habitation does not mean room.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'd like a bedroom with a sea view.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Bedroom is the room you sleep in at home; in a hotel you ask for a room.

ejercicios.explicacion: It is the phrase from the card “Is breakfast included?”. In a question with be, the verb goes before the subject: Is + breakfast + included. As the checker does not take punctuation into account, the affirmative order, Breakfast is included, is also accepted; it is the answer the receptionist would give.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Question with inverted be (Is breakfast included?); as punctuation is not marked, the affirmative is also fine.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿Está incluido el desayuno? / El desayuno está incluido.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The subject breakfast goes between is and the past participle included.
Impossible order in a normal question; is goes first and then the subject.

ejercicios.explicacion: It is the fixed phrase on the card for introducing yourself at a hotel reception. The order is the normal one for an affirmative sentence: subject (I), verb (have), article and noun (a reservation). Note that Spanish “reserva” is reservation when it is the noun; the verb is book.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Phrase for arriving at the hotel.

errores_previstos.explicacion: In English the verb goes after the subject and before the object.
This would be an old-fashioned question; besides, the phrase on arrival is the affirmative one.

ejercicios.frase: Our flight is ___ by forty minutes.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card gives delayed for Spanish “retrasado”. The clue is “by forty minutes”: the preposition by shows how long the delay is (delayed by two hours). Delayed is a past participle that works as an adjective after be. You also hear “forty minutes late”, but the word the card practises and the most common one on departure boards is delayed.
ejercicios.traduccion: Nuestro vuelo lleva cuarenta minutos de retraso.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Calque of Spanish “retrasado”: it is an offensive word for people and is never used for flights.
Delay is the noun or the verb; after is you need the past participle, delayed.
Cancelled means the flight will not happen; a cancelled flight has no minutes of delay.

ejercicios.frase: My sister ___ a lot for work; she's always at airports.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that travel is the verb, and that trip and journey are nouns. The clue is that the gap follows the subject my sister and needs a verb in the present with -s: travels. Neither of the other two words works as a verb with this meaning.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The verb is travel; trip and journey are used as nouns.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi hermana viaja mucho por trabajo; siempre está en aeropuertos.

por_opcion.travels: Correct: travel is the verb; in the present with she it takes -s.
por_opcion.trips: Incorrect: trip is a noun (a journey); as a verb it means “to stumble”, which does not fit.
por_opcion.journeys: Incorrect: journey is a noun (the time spent travelling); as a verb it is very literary and is not used like this.

descripcion_larga_es: This card brings together the words and phrases for travelling: booking (book), getting around airports and stations (gate, platform, boarding pass), staying in a hotel (check in, fully booked) and solving problems (delayed, lost luggage). It is very useful survival vocabulary. It is difficult for Spanish speakers because “perder” can be miss or lose, “viaje” can be trip, journey or travel, and luggage is uncountable.

contexto.que_es: It is the practical vocabulary of travel and accommodation: tickets and bookings, the airport and the train, the hotel and problems. It includes fixed phrasal verbs (check in, check out, take off), uncountable nouns such as luggage and the distinction between travel (verb and concept), trip (a specific journey) and journey (the time spent getting somewhere).
contexto.por_que_importa: These are real situations in which you must understand and make yourself understood quickly: a gate change, a cancelled flight, a room where something is broken. A vocabulary mistake here has practical consequences (“I lost the train” is confusing). Also, travel topics are common in oral tests and reading comprehension texts.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When booking by phone or email, when arriving at a hotel, at the airport or the station and when telling someone about a trip. The signals are the context (gate, flight, room, ticket). Spanish speakers tend to say “a travel”, to use lose for transport, to make luggage plural and to say habitation for “habitación”.
